title: Classroom Activities · Diversity in the Living World
chapter_focus: Observing variety, classifying living things, and appreciating biodiversity.

activities.title: School Garden Walk
activities.objective: Identify plants and animals in the school grounds and group them.
materials: Optional: small magnifying glass per group
Camera or phone for the teacher (to share photos in class later)

steps.title: Brief
steps.detail: Tell students they will silently observe the garden / playground for 15 minutes. They'll list at least 5 plants and 3 animals (including insects). Remind them not to disturb anything.

steps.title: Walk
steps.detail: Walk together. Pause at 3 spots: under a tree, near a flower bed, in an open area. Encourage close observation at each.

steps.title: Field notes
steps.detail: Each student records features: plant — herb/shrub/tree, leaf shape, flower colour. Animal — name, where found, what it was doing.

steps.title: Back in class
steps.detail: Pool the lists. Make a class chart: plant type tally, animal type tally.

guiding_questions: How many different kinds did the whole class find?
Which areas had the most life — and why?
Did anyone find something nobody else did?
What would happen to these living things if we cut all the trees here?
safety_notes: No plucking, picking, or touching insects.
Stay where the teacher can see all students.
variations: Repeat the walk in a different season and compare lists.
If the school has no garden, use a local park, an empty plot, or even a grass patch on the road verge.

activities.title: Sort and Justify
activities.objective: Apply at least two different classification criteria to the same set of organisms.
materials: A printed set of 12 cards, each with a picture and the name of an organism (cow, fish, sparrow, frog, mango, tulsi, neem, rose, ant, lizard, dog, butterfly)
Chart paper and markers per group

steps.title: Round 1
steps.detail: Groups sort all 12 cards into ANY two groups they choose. They paste them on chart paper and write the rule they used at the top.

steps.title: Round 2
steps.detail: Same cards, but they MUST use a different rule than Round 1. They make a second chart.

steps.title: Gallery walk
steps.detail: Charts are stuck on the wall. Groups walk around and try to GUESS the rule each chart used. They write their guesses on a sticky note.

steps.title: Reveal
steps.detail: Each group reads its rule and explains. Discuss which rules were 'fair' (consistent for all 12) and which had exceptions.

guiding_questions: Did any two groups use the same rule? Why might that happen?
Were there cards that were tricky to place? What made them tricky?
Which rule was easiest? Which was the most useful to a biologist?
Would a scientist accept any of these as a real classification? Why or why not?
variations: Add 4 more cards (snake, banyan, moss, mosquito) for advanced groups.
For mixed-ability classes, give one struggling group a starter rule.
